subject: Novus pilot candidate models — post-demo shortlist and rationale
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Novus pilot candidate models — post-demo shortlist and rationale

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Good discussion on the document-classification and entity-normalization flows you’ll run in the pilot. Per our ask at the end of the call, I pulled together a concise candidate shortlist and the operational tradeoffs we should consider for Novus’ expected workload (mixed short doc extraction + follow-up Q&A). See the attachments (novus_benchmarks_summary.csv, novus_prompt_pack_v1.zip) and the short summary below.

Summary of recommendation (shortlist, ordered):
1) vicuna-13b-redwood-q4 (quantized 4-bit) — Primary candidate
   - Why: Best quality on our Novus prompt set (fewer hallucinations on entity normalization), strong throughput with Redwood continuous batching.
   - Latency (median, hosted): ~95ms per token; 99p: ~420ms for long-context paths
   - Cost estimate (hosted): ~$0.45 / 1k tokens (baseline quantized profile)
   - Notes: Good fit for pilot if you need the highest fidelity and can tolerate slightly higher 99p latency.

2) redwood-mistral-lite-8B (int8 runtime) — Cost/latency sweetspot
   - Why: Near parity on extraction F1 in our benchmarks for vanilla prompts, much lower cost and 99p latency.
   - Latency (median, hosted): ~48ms per token; 99p: ~180ms
   - Cost estimate (hosted): ~$0.18 / 1k tokens
   - Notes: Recommend if you expect high concurrency and strict P99 SLOs; watch for occasional edge-case hallucinations on long-tail normalization rules.

3) redwood-flan-xxl (float16) — Conservative/robust option
   - Why: Stable behavior on instruction-following style prompts; slightly higher cost and latency than mistral-lite.
   - Latency (median): ~130ms per token; 99p: ~520ms
   - Cost estimate: ~$0.60 / 1k tokens
   - Notes: Good for safety-sensitive workflows where consistency matters more than peak throughput.

Tradeoff notes and operational suggestions:
- Latency SLOs: If you need <200ms P99, prioritize mistral-lite and use Redwood prefix caching for repeated context fragments.
- Cost targets: quantized vicuna gives best quality per-dollar for medium throughput; mistral-lite delivers the best unit economics at scale.
- Regression guardrails: we recommend a 500-sample regression suite (see prompt_pack) and a small canary run to measure hallucination rate before full rollout.
- Dedicated capacity: if you prefer dedicated GPUs for steady-state throughput, the unit cost gap narrows (~10–20% lower per-token) but requires a 3-month reserved commit to be cost-effective.

Next steps we suggest from Redwood side: share the full benchmark CSV, provide the prompt pack (attached), run a 2-day canary on your dev dataset, and schedule a 30-min follow-up to finalize the pilot target SLOs and acceptance criteria.

I attached the CSV with the raw metrics and a prompt pack containing the 500 canonical test prompts (short/long/document/negative cases). Please confirm the following so we can create the pilot workplan:
- target P99 latency SLO (ms)
- expected peak concurrent requests in pilot
- prioritized acceptance metric (F1 on entities / hallucination rate / user-perceived accuracy)

Happy to jump on a call this week — propose Wed 09/07 10:00 or Thu 09/08 16:00 PT.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: novus_benchmarks_summary.csv (summary), novus_prompt_pack_v1.zip (500 prompts)

Adding a quick internal note / suggestion (Marissa here, ML Ops):

- We should include an explicit regression metric for "entity-normalization hallucination rate" (binary per-sample flag) alongside F1 — Novus cares about canonicalization errors.
- Proposed eval plan (lightweight and automated):
  1) Run 500-sample normalization subset from the prompt_pack (50% real, 50% synthetic edge cases).
  2) Compute: F1_normalize, hallucination_rate, top-1 canonical match rate, latency P50/P99.
  3) If vicuna-13b-quant passes quality thresholds but P99 exceeds target, run quantized-liveness test with 8-bit kernel to see if we can shave p99 without quality loss.
- Canary rollout: 10% traffic for 24 hours, monitor regression metrics and user-fallback rate. If hallucination_rate increases > 1.5x over baseline, auto-fallback to mistral-lite.

I'll attach a short eval_instructions.md with the exact CLI commands and metric scripts — have the analytics team ready to ingest the CSV from the attached benchmarks.

Marissa

2) Dedicated P99: for 120 concurrent streams on a 1-node dedicated pool (A100 equivalent), estimated P99 for vicuna-13b-quant is ~360ms; mistral-lite P99 ~140ms. We’ll include exact profiling outputs if you want a per-pin configuration.

- Action 3 (Both): schedule 30-min follow-up to lock acceptance thresholds and go/no-go criteria. Proposed: Thu 09/08 16:00 PT (if that still works).
